newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow's Vnukovo airport seeking investment.
newsitem.headline: Moscow's Vnukovo airport seeking investment.

text.p: Moscow's second major airport, Vnukovo International, earned a $17.5 million profit last year, but is seeking nearly a half a billion dollars in investment to improve the facility, its top official said on Thursday.
Valery Baranov, Vnukovo's chief executive, told Reuters the airport currently was in talks with "several British banks" about investing in modernisation improvements.
"We hope to get $50 million of investments during this year and $400 million in 1998," he said.
The money was needed, he said, to built up a new international passenger terminal, business passenger lounge and cargo facilities.
Baranov said that Vnukovo's passenger volume was 4.48 million in 1996, the same as the year before, but far below the record of 13.5 million passengers in 1990.
"We earned 100 billion roubles ($17.5 milion) as a balance profit last year," he said.

The airport executive said Vnukovo handled 65,000 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996, which he called "several percent" higher than in the previous year. --Viktor Anoshkin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
